description: End-to-end mass-formula assembly chain: combines the atom Markov-trace chains with the mass-endomorphism tower and CODATA m_e to produce m_p (MeV).  The current pipeline yields ≈ 937.7615 MeV vs CODATA 938.272 MeV (rel_diff ≈ 5.441e-04).  Trust profile is {axiom: 0, mathlib-cited: 0, derived: 2, script-cited: 3, computational: 1} — the SCRIPT_CITED frontier covers the T1+T2+T3+T4 mass-endomorphism tower assembly (currently in mass_endomorphism.py).  This chain is the canonical 'one chain to rule them all' for the proton mass; future PRs push back the script-frontier to make it fully-trusted.

steps.name: Atom Markov-trace tr_M(p, q_0) — from p-tr-M-q0 chain
steps.operation: Reference the existing `p-tr-M-q0.derivation.json` chain, whose target is `tr_M(p, q_0) ≈ 2.1226`.  This step is DERIVED via the chain reference (no script cited).
steps.notes: Derivation chain: p-tr-M-q0.derivation.json (builder: build_atom_tr_M_chains.py).  4 of 5 steps DERIVED via schur-weyl-weight-3 + hoefsmit-rep-21-sigma1 + atomic-braid-recipe-p; only the Markov-trace assembly itself remains SCRIPT_CITED.

steps.name: Atom Markov-trace tr_M(e⁻, q_0) — single-vortex case
steps.operation: The electron is the simplest atomic vortex: a 2-strand (rather than 3-strand) braid for A=1 with no inter-pair crossings.  tr_M(e⁻, q_0) is computed by the same Wenzl-bridge pipeline as the proton (`light_isotope_sweep.py`).  The electron-tower formula additionally specialises to the n=2 case of H_n(q).
steps.notes: script: folio-assistant/computations/light_isotope_sweep.py + mass_endomorphism.py electron-tower path.  SCRIPT_CITED pending its own atom chain (`atom-tr-M-q0` for e⁻ at n_strands=2).

steps.name: m_p_Hecke = T1 + T2 + T3 + T4 (mass-endomorphism tower)
steps.operation:
Per `prop:mass-endomorphism-*`, sum the four Hecke-units tower terms for the proton:
  T1 = |tr_M(T_w(p))|       — descended trace
  T2 = Σ_i Φ_q(|V̂_i|)        — single-generator Φ_q
  T3 = z² · Σ_{i<j} Φ_q(|V̂_i V̂_j|)  — pair Φ_q
  T4 = m_e_Hecke · tr_M(C_dim_q)     — Frobenius co-Casimir
all evaluated in cat-units.
steps.notes: script: folio-assistant/computations/mass_endomorphism.py + proton_mass_tower_derivation.py.  SCRIPT_CITED — the T1+T2+T3+T4 assembly itself awaits its own derivation chain.  Phase A item (50 dps lift) on PR #476 brings each term individually to mpmath precision but does not chain the assembly.

steps.name: m_e_Hecke = T1 + T2 + T3 + T4 (electron mass-endomorphism)
steps.operation: Same tower formula applied to the electron's 2-strand atomic braid.  T4 contribution simplifies because n=2.

steps.name: Dimensionless mass ratio m_p/m_e
steps.operation: Compute the ratio m_p_Hecke / m_e_Hecke.  The framework predicts this ratio dimensionlessly; CODATA fixes the absolute scale via m_e.
steps.notes: Pure arithmetic; one-line ratio of step-3 / step-4 outputs.

steps.name: Scale by CODATA m_e (MeV) → m_p in MeV
steps.operation: m_p (MeV) := (m_p_Hecke / m_e_Hecke) × M_E_MEV.  The absolute-scale input M_E_MEV = 0.51099895 MeV is the **single CODATA-bounded constant** the framework consumes; everything else is derived.
steps.notes: COMPUTATIONAL leaf: m_p_pred ≈ 937.7615 MeV vs CODATA m_p = 938.27208816 MeV.  Current relative error: 5.441e-04 = 544145 ppb (target: 1 ppb, gap of ~6 orders of magnitude).  The gap is the open computational debt covered by Phase A item 1 (precision lift), Phase A item 3 (Term 7 σ_shell), and Phase B (q_0 derivation).
